text: Mari, it's me. I messed up. I need you at the old Vargas garage, right now. Please hurry.
Tomas? Hey, slow down. Stay there, I'm coming.
They took the money I was holding for them. Two guys from the Cuervos. They think I skimmed it.
Did you?
No! I swear. Just get me to Lucha's. She'll know what to do.
Mari... that black car. It's them!
They're shooting at us! Drive, drive!
Hold on to something.
I think we lost them.
Lucha's gonna kill me.
Lucha's gonna feed you. Then she's gonna kill you.
Marisol! Dios mio, what happened to him?
Cuervos. He says he owes them money.
Inside, both of you. Nobody touches my boy under my roof.
Thank you, Lucha. I'll fix this, I swear.
Dex. You look like you slept in a car again.
I did. What have you got for me, Rook?
Green Gatorback. Belongs to a Cuervo lieutenant who stopped paying my cousin's lot. Four months.
A Cuervo. Great. And you want me to walk up and ask for the keys.
I want it here, in one piece. Every dent comes out of your cut. It's parked in Calle Luna, south of the river.
There she is. And there's the welcome committee.
Hey! That's Chuy's ride! Get him!
Nothing personal, fellas. Just business.
Clean getaway. Rook owes me a beer.
Not a scratch. Look at you, a professional.
They had guns, Rook. You didn't mention guns.
Everybody has guns. Listen. The bank has another job. A pickup truck at a boatyard on the river. Ortega's yard.
Boatyard. How hard can a boatyard be.
The truck's at the Ortega boatyard on the river. Bank papers are in the glovebox. In and out, Dex.
In and out. Famous last words.
Step away from my truck. Slowly.
Easy. I'm with the bank. Coastline Savings. You missed four payments.
Coastline bought our loan last month. Then they tripled it. You know who owns Coastline?
I just drive the trucks, lady.
Victor Sandoval. He wants this whole riverfront. And he doesn't care how he gets it.
Look, I'm sorry about your yard, but -
Wait. Hear that? Engines. Those aren't bankers.
Cuervos. With firebombs. You've got friends.
They're here to burn us out. You can run, bank man, or you can help.
Guess I'm helping.
More coming from the bridge!
You didn't have to do that.
Yeah, I did. Dex Calloway. I used to pull people out of the water for a living.
Marisol Ortega. Mari. So. You still taking my truck?
Truck got stolen. Tell the bank. If the Cuervos come back, call me.
Mrs. Paredes, it's a generous offer. Twice what this place is worth.
This place is worth forty years of my life. It is not for sale.
Everything is for sale. The only question is the price, and how long you wait to accept it.
Out. Before I get my frying pan.
Think it over. The neighborhood is changing. Accidents happen.
Let's see who you really work for.
Nice car for a real estate guy.
Hey! Who's there?
The old woman won't sign. The Ortega girl is making noise.
Then make her quiet. My officers won't answer calls from Calle Luna this month.
Mister Sandoval wants the riverfront empty by summer. The Solaris Pier investors are nervous.
Tell Victor his investors can relax. The Cuervos will handle the rest, and my reports will call it gang trouble.
And your fee?
Doubled. Neighborhoods don't burn themselves down.
Holt. The police captain. She's in Sandoval's pocket.
They took him from the bus stop, Mari. In broad daylight. They want the money by tonight.
There is no money, Lucha. He never had it.
The Cuervos keep a stash house on the south side. Anybody they grab ends up there first.
You're coming with me?
I owe your truck an apology. Let's go get your brother.
Your brother always this much trouble?
Since he was six. He's a good kid. He just trusts the wrong people.
Runs in the neighborhood, I guess.
Four, five... more inside. Use the cars for cover.
Clear! Get your brother.
Mari! I knew you'd come. Who's the big guy?
A friend. Can you run?
I can run. Let's go before the rest of them get back.
Company! Get Tomas in a car and get us out of here!
They said the money was never the point. They said Sandoval wants the whole block scared.
Then we make them scared instead.
Repo man! You took my Gatorback. Tonight I take your ride and your dignity.
You stopped paying for it, Chuy. That's how cars work.
Loser signs over his car. Winner takes the pot. Five grand.
Try to keep up.
Who taught this guy to drive?
Pink slip, Chuy. Leave the keys with Rook.
This isn't over. El Cuervo is going to hear about this.
Eat, both of you. Nobody fights on an empty stomach in my diner.
Lucha, the Cuervos said they'd come back. Tonight.
Then we'll be here. Rook lent me something with a bit more bite.
Headlights. Three cars, no plates. Mari...
Everybody down! Lucha, stay behind the counter!
Second car, from the south! Watch the firebombs!
Black SUV. That's him. That's El Cuervo.
Ortega! You and your repo man cost me money. Tonight your diner burns!
Forget this! Drive!
He's running! Grab a car, I'll ride shotgun!
Ram him! Put him into a wall!
He drives like a coward.
Go ahead, Ortega. Pull the trigger. See what happens to your little street.
You don't get to burn us out. Not you. Not Sandoval.
Porto Sol PD! Weapons down. Step away from the suspect.
Captain Holt. Funny. Your officers never answer calls from Calle Luna.
I'll take it from here, Ms. Ortega. Go home. This neighborhood is changing. Change with it.
Mari. Let it go. Not tonight.
So you're the Ortega girl who punched a hole in the Cuervos. Tomas talks about you like you're a superhero.
Tomas talks too much. This is El Cuervo's phone. Can you crack it?
Cheap case, expensive secrets. Give me an hour and a coffee.
Oh no. Hear that? Holt's been trying to pull our license for a year. Somebody tipped her off.
Grab your gear. We're leaving.
Drive! They'll have the whole block covered in a minute.
You know what the worst part is? I was halfway through my best set of the year.
You can finish it in jail if we don't lose them.
Left! No - your other left!
We lost them. Head to the Flats. I keep a backup studio in a garage there. Don't judge.
Okay. El Cuervo is careful, but his phone isn't. Messages from a blocked number. Friday. Club Riptide.
Holt meets Sandoval's accountant in the VIP cabana. If I could get into her phone, we'd have everything.
Then we get into her phone.
Club Riptide. Holt's already in the VIP cabana. She always leaves her jacket on the couch.
Get the chip in the inside pocket and walk out like you own the place. Security will be on the rope.
Walk in, plant it, walk out. Got it.
Now that's a dress. Go on in, miss.
Private party tonight. Not dressed like that.
Well, why didn't you say so. Enjoy your night.
Fine. I'll be back.
Hey! VIP only! Get her!
So much for walking out.
I'm in. Everything on her phone is ours. Now get out of there.
Grey sedan leaving the precinct. That's Holt's bagman. He does two pickups, then takes it all back to her.
Stay on him, stay invisible. When he heads home with the bag, you take it.
Robbing a crooked cop. My favorite kind of Tuesday.
One down. Where to next, pal?
That's the last stop. He's heading back to the precinct.
Nice and easy. Just another car in traffic.
Time to repossess some dirty money.
You're dead! You know whose money this is?
Got it. Oh, that's a lot of money.
Holt's going to be real upset with somebody tonight.
Two hundred grand of Holt's collections, and a ledger with every name that pays her. Kit's going to cry.
Split it with the neighborhood. Lucha's roof needs fixing.
Well, look what the tide dragged in. The Coast Guard's favorite disappointment.
Hello, Jonah. You look old.
I am old. Still alive, though, and that's partly your doing. Don't make that face. I never blamed you for that night.
The Cuervos run airboats through my swamp every evening. Crates of rifles, from a boat in the Gulf.
Guns for Sandoval's little war on Calle Luna. Let's go sink some airboats.
There. Three boats running dark, heading for the old channel. Get me close, I'll do the rest.
Keep her steady! I can't hit a gator at this speed!
You taught me to drive one of these, remember? Hold on.
That's all of them. Their cargo came off that hammock over there. Let's have a look.
Rifles. Enough for a small war. And look at the stencil on the crates.
Solaris Pier Construction. He's not even hiding it.
Men like Sandoval never think they need to hide.
Kit called. The cash boat leaves Port Isle at nine, heads for Key Coral. Two guards, fast hull.
Faster than Dad's old racer? I rebuilt that engine twice.
Nothing's faster than Dad's old racer. Just bring it back in one piece, okay? It's all we have left of him.
I'll bring it back. And a little something extra.
Come on, old girl. Show them what an Ortega engine can do.
There you are. Let's see what you've got.
Money overboard! Grab the bags before they sink.
Sandoval's paying for the new roof on the diner. He just doesn't know it yet.
Blue cab under the gantry cranes, container already on the chassis. Terminal security walks the lanes.
Get in quiet. Once that engine starts, every guard on the island will know.
Quiet is my middle name.
It's actually Raymond. Don't tell anyone.
Intruder in the yard!
Engine's loud. Here they come.
Big truck, small gate. This is going to hurt.
Let's see what's inside... Cash, and ledgers. Solaris Pier Holdings paying the Cuervos, paying Holt.
This is the first piece of real paper we've got on Sandoval himself. Good work, Dex.
Friends. Porto Sol deserves a waterfront that shines. Solaris Pier will bring jobs, light, and a future.
Some people fear change. I say, the tide always comes in. You can swim, or you can drown.
Did he just threaten a whole neighborhood at his own party? I need that on tape. With Holt standing next to him.
End of the pier has the best angle. Stay close to me.
I used to come here as a kid. The coaster was scarier back then.
Perfect. Directional mic is up. Just keep his goons off me for a minute.
Two of his security guys are coming this way. They saw the mic.
More of them! Keep recording!
Got it! Sandoval, Holt, the threats, all of it. Now get me out of here!
Remind me never to go to a party with you again. That was amazing.
Dex... Mayday. They put a hole in my boat. Off Ten Palms. Water's cold... I can't hold on long.
Jonah! Stay with me. Keep your head up. I'm coming.
Haven't flown one of these since the service. It's like riding a bike. A bike that wants to kill you.
Dex, I've got his radio beacon. Southwest of Ten Palms, about a mile out. Hurry.
Four years ago it was a night like this. Two fishermen in the water. I got to one of them.
Not this time. Nobody else drowns on my watch.
Dex! Over here!
Took your sweet time, Coast Guard.
You're welcome. Now hold on, you're going to the hospital.
Dex. Thank you. Now we're even.
Holt's at a police fundraiser downtown until midnight. Her private security walks the grounds.
The safe is in the pool house out back. Crouch, stay in the shadows, and don't let them see you.
A police captain with a villa on Key Coral. Nobody ever asked how.
Intruder! Around the pool!
Is it there? Tell me it's there.
Leather ledger. Dates, amounts, initials. Sandoval's are on every page.
That's it. That's the whole story. Get off that island.
Solaris One. Ninety floors. Sandoval's private vault sits right under the penthouse.
The Calle Luna deeds he stole with fake loans. The Cuervo payroll. And about four million in cash he never declared.
Four million. I'm listening.
We're not doing this for the money, Rook.
Speak for yourself. I've got a retirement to think about.
The deeds are what matter. Every family he pushed out gets their home back.
Then we plan it right. Nobody goes in blind.
First we need eyes on the building. Dex, Mari, go take some pictures. Be tourists.
My father fixed boats for forty years and never owned more than the yard. Sandoval owns a skyline.
Not for long.
Two ways in. Quiet: we dress you as the maintenance crew and walk in the service door.
Loud: we take an armored truck through the loading dock and blow the vault. Your call, Dex.
Quiet it is. I'll find us a van and some very ugly uniforms.
Loud. I was hoping you'd say that. I know an armored truck with a lazy route.
Brightline Facilities keeps its maintenance vans at a depot in the Flats. White van, blue stripe.
Uniforms are in the back. Two guards on the lot, and they will call it in.
Armored truck, leaving Canvas Park on its cash run. Two guards with rifles. Stop it, drag them out, take it.
Got the van. Now to lose the tail.
Big, slow and heavy. Just like my ex.
Beautiful. Four uniforms, one van, zero dignity. We go tomorrow night.
Look at you two. The cleanest window washers in Porto Sol.
I'll loop the cameras from the station. From the service door you'll have twenty minutes, not a second more.
Charges are set to cut the vault door, not the building. Try not to crash before you get there.
Police response to the tower is four minutes. Holt will send everyone she has. Make it quick.
For Calle Luna.
For Calle Luna. Let's go.
Drive like a tired janitor. Slow and sad.
Cameras looping. Elevator to ninety is yours.
Twenty minutes. See you at the top.
Vault's open. Deeds, ledgers, cash, you're golden... wait. Sandoval's head of security just walked into the camera room.
He's seen the loop. The lobby is filling up. Get out, now!
Knock, knock.
Charges are cutting. Sixty seconds. Hold that dock!
Vault's open! Load the cash into the truck and go!
Deeds are in the bag. Drive!
I'm holding every deed in Calle Luna in a gym bag.
Count it later. We got the deeds.
We did it, Dex. We actually did it.
Mija! They took Tomas! Sandoval's men, right out of my kitchen. He says bring everything to Key Solano, or else.
We're coming, Lucha. I promise.
It's a trap, Mari.
Then we spring it.
Sandoval's convoy just got on the Overseas Highway. Four cars. Holt's own cruiser is riding with him.
There they are. Get me alongside, I'll take care of the escorts.
Holt's cruiser is in there too. No more badges between us and him.
Seven miles of bridge and nowhere to hide. Good.
Escorts are done. He's running for Key Solano.
He's running! Tomas, stay down!
You think this changes anything? I own the land, the bank, the police. I own the tide.
You owned a gym bag full of stolen deeds. Now I do.
Mari! You came. You actually came.
Always, little brother.
Porto Sol PD! Nobody move. This is my collar, Ortega. Hand over whatever you took from that tower.
Not to you, Captain. Not ever.
Then we'll see whose story this city believes.
Funny you say that. We know a DJ.
It's all here. The tape from the pier. Holt's ledger. The deeds. Sandoval's books. I can go live in two minutes.
Or we sell it back. Holt would pay anything to make this go away. The yard, the diner, money for all of us.
Money comes and goes, mija. The neighborhood remembers what you did with it.
Your call, Mari. Whatever you decide, I'm with you.
Think it'll stick?
It's on the radio. Everybody heard it. That sticks.
Stay for dinner. Lucha's making pozole.
Wouldn't miss it.
Two million dollars. The yard's yours. Nobody's losing their home.
And Holt is still wearing a badge.
We won, Mari. Mostly. Keep the copies somewhere safe.
Somewhere safe. In this town. That'll be the day.
Put it on the air, Kit. All of it.
Pulse FM, this is Kit Navarro, and tonight's show is about the people who sold our city. Stay tuned.
Here come Holt's loyalists. Everybody find cover.
Call Holt. Tell her the Sol Beach Pier. Tonight. Come alone.
She won't come alone.
I know.
It's out. Every station in the state is picking it up. They can't stop it now.
You have something of mine, Ortega.
I have a lot of things of yours. Two million dollars. Every deed back where it belongs. And you never set foot in Calle Luna again.
Two million. Fine. The money is already moving. Pleasure doing business.
Take them.
Knew it!
Impressive. The money is in your account, Ortega. Keep your copies safe. I'll keep my badge.
Stay out of my neighborhood, Captain.
Hey, Dex. Just checking in.
I need you for something. Come find me, it's marked on your map. We call it %s.
I'll be there.
